about: The register of known risks (spec §50, risk_register): what the expert panel found on 19 Oct 2026, and the owner's decision on each. The release waits on it: scripts/risk-register.mjs --release fails on an open fix-now risk, an overdue fix-later one, or one whose files moved since it was reviewed. RELEASING.md, "Known risks", says how a risk is cleared.

panel.about: The last time every role looked at the whole project. A release that starts a new version line (0.7 to 0.8) waits for a new one.

risks.title: Python library runs note guards through eval
risks.risk: A guard text in a graph note, such as `__import__('os').system(...)`, runs as Python when the library joins or steps that graph. Anyone who opens a shared note with the Python library runs the note author's code.
risks.fix: Replace the three eval calls with a small parser of comparisons joined by and, or and not. Validate.js:7 already does this in JavaScript. Reject anything else.
risks.check: A unit test feeds a guard that calls __import__ and asserts a refusal. Add ruff rule S307 (eval) to pyproject so a new eval fails lint.

risks.title: SECURITY.md promises rest on settings nothing in CI checks
risks.risk: SECURITY.md says CodeQL runs on each pull request and secret push protection blocks leaks. Both are GitHub settings with no workflow in the repository. The script that checks them (--settings) runs only by hand, so the promises can silently stop being true after the repository went public.
evidence: unverified: no .github/workflows/codeql*.yml exists; the CodeQL default setup state could not be read from the repository
risks.fix: Run `public-readiness.mjs --settings` in release.yml and in a weekly job. Use a token that can read repository security settings. Fail the run when any wanted setting differs.
risks.check: That job itself; release-check.yml runs it too so a drift is seen before the tag.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.title: Claude's data-folder guard admits a bypass by shell paths
risks.risk: settings.json in the mod's data folder sets Claude's own classification ceiling. The guard says it cannot see a path the shell builds (cd then a bare name, or an unlisted variable). A prompt-injected session could loosen its own gate and then open a note classified above it.
risks.fix: Record the digest of settings.json when the session starts. Have the gate refuse to open any note when the file's digest has changed during the session, until the person confirms.
risks.check: A test in packages/claude-code/test that rewrites settings.json mid-session and asserts the next /graph edit is refused.
risks.wave: Wave 11 · Slice 8 permissions, AI and export

risks.title: Session token drawn in a pane Claude may read
risks.risk: The page address with the session token is handed to the Graph editor pane to draw, and the spec says Claude can read that pane. With the token, Claude could PUT the note directly and skip the proposal-only route the person is meant to accept.
evidence: unverified: whether the pane that draws the link is among the panes put into Claude's context
risks.fix: Have the mod open the browser itself, or draw a button whose target is held outside pane text. Then the token never appears in any text Claude can read.
risks.check: A test asserts no pane text and no transcript line ever contains `token=`.
risks.wave: Wave 11 · Slice 8 permissions, AI and export

risks.title: Nightly pre-release is not attested
risks.risk: The stable release carries a build provenance attestation, but the nightly only ships a SHA256SUMS made by the same job. A BRAT user following nightlies cannot tell a genuine build from a tampered one.
risks.fix: Add the same attest-build-provenance step (with id-token and attestations write) to the nightly build job for main.js, manifest.json and styles.css.
risks.check: A workflow test (as test/build-status-run.test.js does for its script) asserts nightly.yml names the attest action.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.title: Store assets are never rebuilt and compared
risks.risk: Nothing builds main.js twice or rebuilds a tag and diffs it against the released file. A reviewer or user cannot confirm the Obsidian store asset matches the source, and a non-deterministic build would go unnoticed.
evidence: unverified: any reproducibility step in release.yml, release-check.yml or scripts/
risks.fix: In release-check.yml build twice in separate clean checkouts and fail when the sha256 of main.js, styles.css or the tarball differs.
risks.check: That release-check step, and a documented `npm run build && sha256sum main.js` line in RELEASING.md for anyone to repeat.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.title: SCXML parsed with lxml's default entity handling
risks.risk: The library parses SCXML text with etree.fromstring and no parser settings. A crafted file with an external entity can read a local file into the document. Only someone handed an untrusted SCXML file is exposed.
risks.fix: Parse with `etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True, huge_tree=False)` in both places.
risks.check: A unit test parses a document with an external entity and asserts the entity is not expanded; ruff rule S320 flags a bare lxml parse.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.title: Two personal tokens live in workflows with unverified scope
risks.risk: PROJECT_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are the maintainer's own tokens, used by jobs with issues or pull-requests write. Their scopes, expiry and rotation are not recorded anywhere in the repository. A leak through a future action change would not be bounded by design.
evidence: unverified: token scopes and expiry, which only the GitHub settings show
risks.fix: Make PROJECT_TOKEN a fine-grained token limited to the project and this repository, with an expiry. Note each secret's scope, owner and renewal date in RELEASING.md.
risks.check: manual
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.title: Export accepts any text under an .svg name
risks.risk: The export route checks a PNG's bytes but writes any text given as .svg, .md, .csv or .graphml. If the page were ever compromised, it could drop an SVG with a script into the vault, which runs when opened in a browser. The panel proposes accepting this risk; the owner decides.
risks.fix: If wanted: refuse an .svg whose text holds <script, on* attributes, <foreignObject or a javascript: address, as a second line behind the page's CSP.
risks.check: A test PUTs an SVG with a script element and asserts 400.
risks.wave: Roger’s held changes, after all waves

risks.title: No advisory audit for the Python dependencies in CI
risks.risk: npm audit signatures and dependency-review cover JavaScript, but nothing audits pyyaml, lxml and rfc8785 against published advisories except Dependabot's weekly alert. A known hole in lxml would stay in a shipped tarball until the next Dependabot pass.
evidence: unverified: pip-audit, uv audit or osv-scanner in any workflow
risks.fix: Add `uvx pip-audit --locked` (or osv-scanner on uv.lock) to the Python job in ci.yml and release.yml.
risks.check: That CI step.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: One person holds every key, with no written recovery
risks.risk: If the owner is unavailable, nobody can publish a release or change the ruleset. Nobody can rotate PROJECT_TOKEN or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, or renew the thoughtknot.app domain. Nothing in the repository says what those keys are, where they live, or how a successor would recover them.
evidence: unverified: any recovery, backup or hand-over document; any second admin or organisation owner; where the thoughtknot.app DNS is held
risks.fix: Add a 'Keys and recovery' section to RELEASING.md. Name each secret, its scope, where it is made and its expiry. Name the Pages domain's registrar and the one command that re-applies settings. Name a second admin on the repository, or move it to an organisation with two owners.
risks.check: manual

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: A tag on any commit becomes a stable release
risks.risk: The release workflow runs for a bare version tag pushed on any commit, not only one on main. A tag typed on the wrong branch or a stale checkout ships code that never passed the dry run or the required checks.
evidence: unverified: a tag ruleset on GitHub that limits who may push a version tag
risks.fix: Add a first step to the release job: fetch origin/main and fail unless the tagged commit is its head (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` at least). Put the manifest check before `npm test`, so a wrong tag fails in seconds.
risks.check: A case in test/policy.test.js that the release job's first run step compares HEAD with origin/main before any install.

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: No written release steps, draft publishing or rollback
risks.risk: RELEASING.md holds only the accessibility walk. It never says to bump manifest.json, versions.json and every package.json, run the dry run, push the tag, then publish the draft. A draft left unpublished tells no one, and a bad release has no written way back.
evidence: unverified: a rebuild from a tag giving a byte-identical main.js; the release notes depend on the day's OSV and NVD answers (release.yml:36, 108)
risks.fix: Add a numbered 'Cutting a release' list and a 'Going back' paragraph to RELEASING.md. A bad release is followed by a patch, the draft is deleted, the tag stays. Add an `npm run release:prepare` that bumps the three version files together.
risks.check: A scheduled step in pages.yml or build-status.yml that warns when a draft release is older than one day.

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Every job without a time limit can hold a runner six hours
risks.risk: CI's seven jobs, all three nightly jobs, the release and public-readiness jobs, dependency review, advisories and the lock job set no timeout-minutes. A hung `npm ci`, `gh` call or Chrome blocks runners for six hours each, and a stuck nightly holds the concurrency group until then.
risks.fix: Give every job a timeout-minutes, about twice its usual length (CI 30, nightly build 40, release 60).
risks.check: A case in test/policy.test.js that every job in every workflow has `timeout-minutes`.

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: The release waits on live OSV and NVD, with no retry
risks.risk: The release's quality job calls OSV and NVD once each and throws on any non-200 answer. An NVD outage or rate limit, which are common, fails the release after an hour of Cachegrind, and the version number is spent.
risks.fix: Retry each call three times with backoff. When a source still fails, use the committed cache if it was checked within 14 days, and print a warning instead of failing. Move the refresh before the Valgrind install so a failure is cheap.
risks.check: A test in test/engine-version.test.js with a fetch that answers 503 once, then 200.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Failures of nightly, wiki, Pages and advisories are silent
risks.risk: No workflow tells anyone when it fails; only GitHub's default e-mail to the owner does, and only if their settings allow it. The build-status board follows CI and stable releases alone, so a nightly or wiki that has failed for a month shows nowhere.
evidence: unverified: the owner's GitHub notification settings for failed scheduled runs
risks.fix: Add a small `report` job (`if: failure()`, `issues: write`) that opens or updates one issue labelled `workflow-failure`, reusing the pattern in wiki.yml's report job.
risks.check: A case in the workflow tests that every scheduled workflow has a failure-reporting job.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Timed workflows pause and tokens expire without notice
risks.risk: GitHub turns off scheduled workflows after 60 days with no commit. A quiet spell then stops the nightly, the daily Pages rebuild, the lock job and the advisory watch. PROJECT_TOKEN is a classic token whose expiry is unrecorded, and an expired one only warns, so the board goes stale unseen.
evidence: unverified: PROJECT_TOKEN's expiry date and whether it has one
risks.fix: Record each secret's expiry in RELEASING.md and set a calendar reminder two weeks before. Make the build-status warning open an issue after three refused runs in a row.
risks.check: A monthly scheduled job that calls the project API with PROJECT_TOKEN and fails loudly on 401.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Repository settings are not exported; only required checks are held
risks.risk: The code holds the required checks list, but not the ruleset's other rules. Those are: pull request required, merge commits only, bypass actors, CodeQL as a check, Pages source and domain. A setting changed by hand or by GitHub drifts with nothing to compare against, and `--settings` runs only when an admin remembers.
evidence: unverified: any exported ruleset JSON in the repository
risks.fix: Add `--settings --export` that writes the full default-branch ruleset and the Pages settings to `.github/settings/`. Have `--settings` compare the whole ruleset, not one rule. Run it before each release as a RELEASING.md step.
risks.check: A release-check step that runs `public-readiness.mjs --settings` with a fine-grained admin token stored for that job alone, or manual.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Docker base, uv and Node pins are never bumped; no SBOM
risks.risk: Dependabot watches npm, uv and Actions, but not the Docker image digest, the setup-uv `version:` input or the exact Node 24.20.0. These age silently until a security fix or a retired image forces a hurried change. A release ships checksums and provenance but no SBOM, so a user cannot list what is inside main.js.
risks.fix: Add a `docker` entry to dependabot.yml. Add a release step that writes `npm sbom --sbom-format cyclonedx` to an asset and attests it. Note in CONTRIBUTING.md that the Node patch and setup-uv version are bumped by hand with a new baseline.
risks.check: A case in test/policy.test.js that dependabot.yml names docker, and that the release's asset list includes the SBOM.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: A runner change or one flaky test blocks the release
risks.risk: Instruction counts are held only to the same OS, processor, Node major and Valgrind, with 5% tolerance. The measured spread is never committed or compared with that tolerance. When GitHub moves ubuntu-24.04 to new hardware, the release fails. It also fails when the baseline's flaky_tests of 0 meets one flaky test in the double run. It then waits for a new baseline pull request.
evidence: unverified: whether the machine match includes the CPU model (quality/baseline.json:47) or only the architecture
risks.fix: Commit `largest_spread` with each baseline and have quality-check fail a baseline whose tolerance is under twice it. Write in RELEASING.md the recovery order: run Quality baseline, commit it, re-run the dry run, then tag.
risks.check: A case in test/quality-baseline.test.js that the committed baseline carries a spread and that INSTRUCTION_TOLERANCE is at least twice it.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Wiki and Pages depend on Chrome being on the runner image
risks.risk: Both page builders call `google-chrome` from the ubuntu-latest image, which GitHub may drop or move. Pages only warns and ships without the picture, but the wiki job fails outright on every push to main, and the whole wiki stops updating.
risks.fix: Give the wiki step the same `|| echo ::warning::` fallback as pages.yml, and keep the last published images when a screenshot fails.
risks.check: A case in test/wiki-workflow or test/site-workflow that the screenshot step never fails the job.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: IT administrator and release / DevOps engineer
risks.title: Docs disagree with the workflows on schedules and write access
risks.risk: CONTRIBUTING says the advisory watch's weekly schedule is off, but the workflow has a cron. The README says only the release job may write, while seven other jobs write releases, the wiki, Pages, issues or pull requests. A successor reading the docs will misjudge what runs and what can change the repository.
risks.fix: Correct the two sentences, and add a one-table 'Who may write what' to CONTRIBUTING.md listing each job's write permission and why.
risks.check: A case in test/policy.test.js that every job with a write permission is named in that table.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: The graph-spec library is not type-checked at all
risks.risk: The 5,185-line JavaScript library that reads, checks and lays out every graph runs with checkJs off. No file of its 42 has @ts-check. A wrong argument or a renamed field is found only by a test or a user, while CONTRIBUTING says TypeScript is strict in every package.
risks.fix: Turn on checkJs with JSDoc types file by file. Start with reader/store.js, joins/merge3.js and graph-layout.js. Keep the tsconfig at checkJs true once they pass.
risks.check: A conventions test that fails when any package tsconfig under typecheck has checkJs false or allowJs without checkJs.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: merge3, 306 untyped lines, is proved by one snapshot case
risks.risk: The three-way join of two documents over a base is the longest function in the repository. Its only tests are one characterisation case replayed against expected.json and a check that the name is exported. A wrong merge that still matches the old recorded answer, or any new branch of the function, passes unseen.
risks.fix: Add a joins test file with behaviour cases written as inputs and expected rows. Write one for each branch merge3 takes (agree, one side changed, both changed, hold on and off). Share them with the Python tests through cases.mjs.
risks.check: Line coverage of packages/graph-spec/src/joins/** added to quality-suite.mjs with a floor in quality/baseline.json.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: Coverage is measured for the core only, and only at release
risks.risk: The 99.2% figure in quality/baseline.json covers packages/core/src alone. The Obsidian plugin, the server and the page have no coverage number at any time. CI runs quality-check with --fast, so a pull request that drops the core's coverage is seen only when a release is cut.
risks.fix: Widen --test-coverage-include to packages/*/src, packages/claude-code/server and page. Record one baseline per package. Run the coverage step in CI on pull requests that touch a package.
risks.check: quality-check.mjs holds each package's coverage_percent against its baseline on every pull request, not only at release.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: The Claude Code mod is outside typecheck, lint and CI
risks.risk: register.tsx (265 lines) starts the server, runs Graphviz and refuses Claude's own writes into the data folder. Yet CI never type-checks, lints or runs its test. The guide asks for a manual `claude plugin test` before a merge, so a broken hook ships when someone forgets.
risks.fix: Add `tsc -p packages/claude-code/mod --noEmit` to the typecheck script. Add a release-check step that runs `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin test` where the CLI is installed. Make it fail when the CLI is not installed.
risks.check: A CI job with the Claude Code CLI that runs the mod's test. Until then, a conventions test that register.tsx imports nothing but src/ modules already under test.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: No test runs vault.process with a real interleaving
risks.risk: The code defends against a stale write well. Every write passes through vault.process and is refused when the block text differs from the one last read. But the test shim applies the process callback synchronously. So no test can place a keystroke or a vault change between the read and the write, where Obsidian's asynchronous process really runs.
risks.fix: Give the shim's process an awaited read and an awaited write with a hook between them. Add one test for each writer that changes the note in that gap. It expects a refusal and a kept draft.
risks.check: A test in pane-writing.test.js and block tests that uses the gap hook. The conventions test lists the shim as a file the plugin's tests load.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: 77 fixed sleeps remain in 26 plugin test files
risks.risk: The ratchet stops new sleeps but keeps the old ones, 10 in settings.test.js and 8 in graph-view-parked.test.js. On a slow CI runner one of these fails now and then. The full suite is never skipped before a merge, so a release waits on a rerun.
risks.fix: Replace each sleep with the test support's `until` on the state asserted, one file per pull request, and run --tighten after each.
risks.check: The existing fixed-sleeps ratchet, plus a quality metric that fails when the total allowance stops falling across two releases.
risks.wave: Wave 5 · Automated quality and releases

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: 139 of 249 core modules have no test named after them
risks.risk: Files up to 389 lines, such as proposals-review.ts, style-graph.ts, link-scan.ts and style-checks.ts, are reached only through other modules' tests. Line coverage says those lines ran, not that their answers were asserted, so a wrong branch in one can pass while the suite stays green.
risks.fix: Add a ratchet file of core modules with no named test. Require a new module over 100 lines to have one. Work the list down, starting with the four named.
risks.check: A conventions test that fails when the list of unnamed modules grows, in the style of test/fixed-sleeps.json.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: Reader parity rests on a small, snapshot-shaped case set
risks.risk: The JavaScript and Python readers are held to each other through cases.mjs and 25 recorded answers in expected.json. The test says these were recorded before the code moved here. The shared behaviour files are thin, two reading cases and two problem-code cases. So both readers can agree and still be wrong on a shape neither case holds.
risks.fix: Grow reading-cases.json and problem-code-cases.json with one case per reader rule. Write each with its intended answer rather than a recorded one. Have both readers run them.
risks.check: A test that every problem code in reader/problem-codes.json has at least one case in problem-code-cases.json.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: 28 functions over 100 lines; the 400-line cap is on files
risks.risk: No module passes 400 lines. But renderProperties (272 lines), renderBlock (221), renderViewBlock (217) and bindViewportEvents (203) are single functions that nobody can hold in their head. A change in one is hard to review, and its branches are hard to test one by one.
risks.fix: Add a function-length rule to the conventions test with a ratchet of the functions now over 100 lines. Split the four named when they are next touched.
risks.check: A conventions test over the TypeScript AST that fails when a function over 100 lines is added or one on the list grows.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: Live Preview hands a hand-made context to the block renderer
risks.risk: The editing view builds a five-field object and casts it to MarkdownPostProcessorContext, the plugin's one unchecked cast of an Obsidian type. When Obsidian adds a field the renderer or a child reads, the card in Live Preview fails. The reading view keeps working, and the compiler cannot say so.
risks.fix: Give renderShown a narrow interface of the fields it uses (sourcePath, getSectionInfo, addChild). Pass Obsidian's context or the hand-made one to that type, without a cast.
risks.check: The typecheck, once the cast is gone; a conventions test that counts `as unknown as` in packages/obsidian/src and holds it at zero.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: A running layout is never cancelled when the user keeps typing
risks.risk: A new edit replaces only layouts still queued for the same owner. The one already in the worker runs to its end, and its result is then dropped as stale. On a large graph each keystroke waits behind a layout nobody wants, so the drawing lags further the more the person types. The panel proposes accepting this risk; the owner decides.
risks.fix: When a newer job for the same owner arrives while its earlier one is busy, terminate and restart the worker. The timeout path already does this. Do not wait for the old job.
risks.check: manual
risks.wave: Roger’s held changes, after all waves

risks.role: Senior coder and QA / test engineer
risks.title: The server keeps no copy of the note it overwrites
risks.risk: The write is atomic and fsynced, so a crash leaves the old or the new note whole. But the earlier text is kept only when the note's folder is a git repository. Take a note outside git where a good write carried a bad edit. It has no earlier version the changes view or the person can go back to. The panel proposes accepting this risk; the owner decides.
risks.fix: Before the rename, copy the note's current bytes into the drafts folder under its digest name as a one-deep 'before' record. Offer it in the changes view when git has no history.
risks.check: manual
risks.wave: Roger’s held changes, after all waves

risks.title: Host contract covers display only; files and settings copied per host
risks.risk: The Tauri app (Wave 7) and VS Code (Wave 8) will each hand-copy about 600 lines of glue. This covers notes, drafts, settings and the layout worker. No shared test holds it. Every later change to how a note is read or written then has to be made three or four times, and drifts.
risks.fix: Before H1 (Wave 7), widen the published host interface to what the requirement names: note store, drafts, settings, secrets and the layout runner. Give each one a contract check in host-contract.ts. Make the Obsidian and page adapters pass it in test/host-adapters.test.js.
risks.check: test/host-adapters.test.js runs every adapter against every contract check. A conventions rule fails a host package that defines its own note read or write outside the adapter.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.title: Storage interface exists only as EditorNote, with no contract suite
risks.risk: Sync (Wave 13), the encrypted store (W30) and the GitHub backend (Wave 27) are all planned as 'one more backend of the storage interface'. But that interface has no file and no contract test. It has two hand-written implementations. Whoever adds the third backend inherits the differences between the first two.
risks.fix: In Wave 6 (L1) lift EditorNote plus a small NoteStore (read, write-if-unchanged, watch, list, draft) into core as the named storage interface. Write test/storage-contract.test.js. Run the vault, the page store and a plain-folder backend against it before the Tauri app starts.
risks.check: storage-contract.test.js in the suite, listed in CONTRIBUTING.md, with every backend registered; the requirement flips to written only with all three.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.title: Layering is not held across packages; hosts reach into core internals
risks.risk: The page imports 55 core modules by relative path in 15 files, bypassing the package's exports map and the public-api check. A core refactor that keeps the public surface still breaks the Claude Code host, and the planned layers test does not exist.
risks.fix: Add test/layers.test.js now: every import outside packages/core that names core must go through @thoughtknot/core, its display/* or hosts/* paths. Export what the page needs from the entry. Replace the relative imports.
risks.check: test/layers.test.js in the suite, built on scripts/import-graph.mjs, failing any ../core/src or ../graph-spec/src import from a host package.
risks.wave: Wave 6 · Host, storage and plug-in contracts

risks.title: The note format carries no version and has no migration story
risks.risk: A block is identified only by '// graph: name' with no profile version. Waves 9 to 13 add type, time, provenance and CRDT-merged text. Then an older app cannot tell a newer block from a broken one. Two peers on different versions silently disagree.
evidence: unverified: any 'migrate', 'upgrade' or 'newer format' rule in packages/graph-spec/src, python/graph_spec/src or the requirements
risks.fix: Before Wave 9, add an optional profile version to the graph line or GraphMeta. Add a rule that a reader refuses a newer major plainly and keeps the bytes. Write one requirement for how a schema moves from decision@1 to decision@2.
risks.check: A shared case table (reader-cases.json) with a newer-version block that both readers refuse with the same GN code; problem-codes.test.mjs holds the code.
risks.wave: Wave 9 · Slice 6 the mesh

risks.title: Two hand-kept parsers, no grammar; drift caught only on listed cases
risks.risk: The JavaScript and Python readers are written separately (parser.js 235 lines, grammar.py 268 lines). They agree only on the case tables and the parity runs. A syntax added to one and not the other ships unnoticed. So does an edge the tables miss. It shows only when a Python tool and the editor read one note differently.

risks.risk: The server gets its gate settings and the digest of a note the person confirmed through its environment. Another process of the same user can read them, or start the server with its own.

risks.risk: The AI scope takes in the vault's shared schemas, but only the class of the note being asked about is checked. A schema kept in a note of a higher class can be sent.

risks.title: Plug-ins run with the host's full powers
risks.risk: A plug-in runs in the same process as the host, so it can reach the network and the host's calls whatever its manifest says. Its time is read only after a call returns, so a call that never returns, or work it starts and leaves running, is not stopped. No host loads outside plug-ins yet, so this matters once one does.
risks.fix: Do this before any host loads a plug-in it did not ship. Run plug-ins in a worker that gets only the extension points, and stop one that runs too long.
risks.check: packages/core/test/plugins-isolated.test.js: a plug-in that loops or never answers is stopped and named, its worker has no network, and it reaches only the host abilities it names.

risks.title: A plug-in given secrets could read every secret, AI keys too
risks.risk: The secrets ability handed a plug-in the host's whole secret store. Any plug-in that named it could read the key of every AI model the person set up, and the secrets of every other plug-in.
risks.fix: Give each plug-in only the secrets named under its own id, such as acme.one.token. Any other name gives null, and the host is never asked for it.
risks.check: packages/core/test/plugins-limits.test.js: a plug-in asking for an AI key, another plug-in's secret or a name that only starts like its id gets null, and the host is asked for none of them.

risks.title: The files ability reaches every note, whatever its class
risks.risk: A plug-in given the files ability reads and writes every note through the host's storage. Nothing checks a note's class, so a plug-in can read a note the person keeps from AI and from other people.
risks.fix: Do this before a host loads an outside plug-in. Give the files ability through the note gate. A plug-in reads only notes at or below a ceiling the person sets for it. Its writes go to a proposal card.
risks.check: packages/core/test/plugins-limits.test.js: a plug-in lists and reads only notes at or below its ceiling. A write it makes waits for the person.

risks.title: Comments and tags taken out in one pass
risks.risk: Taking out comments or tags in one pass can leave a new one made from the pieces round each removed part. The drawing and the test report each did so.

risks.title: A test checked a web address by part of its text

risks.risk: The flat projection set keys from names in the graph. A relationship or a property named __proto__ changed an object's prototype instead of being kept.

risks.risk: The reflow check built code for a page from button labels with JSON alone. A label with a closing script tag or a line separator could break out of it.

risks.title: The desktop app's Linux build carries glib 0.18, with a known unsoundness
risks.risk: Advisory GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g (moderate): an iterator in glib 0.18, VariantStrIter, is unsound. Tauri draws Linux windows with GTK 3, which pins glib 0.18. The fix is in glib 0.20, which needs GTK 4. Tauri has no GTK 4 release yet.
risks.fix: When Tauri supports GTK 4, bump glib to 0.20 or later. Then remove GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g from allow-ghsas in .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml, and close this risk.

risks.accepted_reason: No code in the app's dependencies calls VariantStrIter. It is the Linux build only. No fixed glib works with Tauri yet. Undo when Tauri supports GTK 4.
